authorization: User approved the operating-point reset and prospective evaluation change in this chat on 2026-11-18.

roles.F: Original R30 fitting; no new access or fitting needed.
roles.V: Original R30 checkpoint selection; frozen, no new operating-point search.
roles.C: All original 5511 normal calibration rows per model; thresholds use only these cached scores.
roles.ED: Already-open 17059-row development evaluation; never used to set rank, alpha, delta or select a model.
roles.independent_confirmation: Not ready; candidate source eligibility is reviewed separately. No claim of a new blind test.

methods.formula: min k in 1..n such that Binomial(n,1-alpha).sf(k-1)<=delta
methods.role: Existing standard calibration reference, not a new 2025/2026 algorithm or TLNP reproduction.

decision.scope: one shared threshold per model across all 15 ED units

stopping: Exactly one new fixed calibration reference; no alpha/delta/rank grid.
Any unit violation means this reference does not satisfy that model's declared development risk target; report and end this comparison.
Even if all development units pass, only retain a candidate for independent evaluation; do not select a winning seed or claim deployment risk control.
No automatic subgroup training, model replacement, fusion, new data collection or recalibration candidate after the result.
limitations: The original ED labels and feasibility bounds were already examined before this design; this is a post-hoc development comparison, not pristine preregistration.
The rule and constants are fixed before computing its new threshold values and ED decisions.

The NP binomial reference assumes an independent fixed scorer and iid normal calibration from the target normal distribution; repeated development use, correlated flows and B-to-D shift prevent asserting that theorem here.
The pointwise nominal delta does not establish simultaneous 15-unit or three-seed finite-sample FPR guarantees.
Feasible intervals derived using ED labels are diagnostic-only and never enter calibration.
